findings.title: update() compares against the organization-aware wrapped model, causing missed login-cache invalidations when the IDP's organization is disabled
findings.body: In update(), the 'original' model used by registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is obtained via getById(), which returns the model wrapped by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. That wrapper overrides isEnabled() to also require the linked organization to be enabled. getLoginPredicate() (LoginFilter.ENABLED) calls isEnabled(), so when an IDP's organization is currently disabled, predicate(original) evaluates to false even though the IDP itself is a valid login IDP. Now consider this sequence: (1) an org-linked public IDP is in the cached getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL) ID list; (2) the organization is disabled; (3) the admin updates the IDP to make it unavailable for login — sets hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true, or broker_public=false — while keeping it enabled. predicate(updated) is false, and because predicate(original) is also false (due to the disabled org, not the IDP), registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate hits the first 'both false' branch and registers NO invalidation of the .idp.login.* caches. The IDP's internal id therefore stays in the cached login ID sets. (4) When the organization is re-enabled (which does not invalidate the login caches, by design), getForLogin serves the stale cached id, getById returns a wrapper whose isEnabled() is now true, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled() — it does not re-check hideOnLogin, linkOnly, or BROKER_PUBLIC in the ORG_ONLY/ALL paths — so a broker the admin explicitly hid or made private is displayed and usable on the login pages. The fix is to compute the original login-eligibility from the raw delegate model (or an unwrapped copy) rather than from the organization-aware wrapper, so org enablement does not poison the comparison.

findings.title: Test cleanup registers removal of literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases
findings.body: In the new testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup is registered as getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) (lines 381 and 425; the same copy-paste bug exists in the pre-existing testCacheIDPByOrg at line 303). The literal string "alias" is used instead of the actual alias variable (e.g. "idp-alias-" + i). As a result the 21 identity providers created by this test (idp-alias-0 … idp-alias-20) are never removed, while teardown attempts to delete a non-existent IDP with alias "alias". The leaked, mostly enabled IDPs persist in the shared "test" realm and can pollute subsequent tests in the class and other test classes that count or render identity providers for that realm. The cleanup should reference the created alias, e.g. final String alias = "idp-alias-" + i; getCleanup().addCleanup(() -> testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias).remove()).
